cluster_name: New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) and non-animal data

findings.claim: A NAM economic analysis in the paper's body estimates that replacing animal DILI evaluation with liver-on-chip could save ~$3 billion annually.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Switching to liver-on-chip for DILI evaluations could save approximately $3 billion annually by enhancing productivity through earlier and more reliable predictions.
findings.evidence: Body (Results/Discussion) of a review modelling NAM impact on preclinical drug development; frames organ-on-chip as economically superior for drug-induced liver injury prediction.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Switching to liver-on-chip for DILI evaluations could save approximately $3 billion annually by enhancing productivity through earlier and more reliable predictions.
findings.study_system: in silico + microphysiological (organ-on-chip) NAMs in preclinical drug development

findings.claim: hiPSC-derived cardiac organoids and heart organoids show measurable, differing spontaneous beating efficiencies during differentiation, quantifying model reproducibility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Notably, COs showed a beating efficiency of 68.1%, whereas HOs exhibited a lower rate of 34.5% on day 8 of differentiation.
findings.evidence: Body (Results) of a primary study building hiPSC multi-cellular heart organoids to model acute myocardial infarction and cardiac fibrosis as an animal alternative.
findings.effect_size: 68.1% (cardiac organoids) vs 34.5% (heart organoids) beating efficiency at day 8
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Notably, COs showed a beating efficiency of 68.1%, whereas HOs exhibited a lower rate of 34.5% on day 8 of differentiation.
findings.study_system: human iPSC-derived heart organoids (cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial cells)

findings.claim: A QSAR-ICE-SSD in silico pipeline for aquatic toxicity achieved high internal reliability, with most interspecies models passing cross-validation, supporting predictions without new in vivo testing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: All models had a cross- validation success rates > 75%, with 74% (17 models) of the models having a cross- validation success rates > 80%, indicating that all of models with the high reliability (;).
findings.evidence: Body (Results) of a primary in silico study combining QSAR, interspecies correlation estimation and species sensitivity distribution to derive hazardous concentrations for alkylphenols.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: All models had a cross- validation success rates > 75%, with 74% (17 models) of the models having a cross- validation success rates > 80%, indicating that all of models with the high reliability (;).
findings.study_system: in silico QSAR-ICE-SSD models for aquatic organisms (alkylphenols)

findings.claim: A microfluidic liver-islet multi-organoid system maintained high cell viability over 30-day culture, demonstrating a functional human-relevant NAM for type 2 diabetes.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A high proportion of the liver (≈99.03%) and islet (≈96.11%) organoid cells were viable (FigureD,E, Supporting Information), indicating that the liver and islet organoids maintained favorable morphology and cell viability during development.
findings.evidence: Body (Results) of a primary study building a hiPSC liver-pancreatic-islet organoid-on-chip to model the liver-islet axis in normal and diabetic states.
findings.effect_size: ~99.03% liver and ~96.11% islet organoid cell viability
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A high proportion of the liver (≈99.03%) and islet (≈96.11%) organoid cells were viable (FigureD,E, Supporting Information), indicating that the liver and islet organoids maintained favorable morphology and cell viability during development.
findings.study_system: human iPSC-derived liver + pancreatic islet multi-organoid microfluidic chip

findings.claim: A scoping review of FAIR data in health research found most FAIRification efforts report on infrastructure/tools and outcomes, but the field is young and adoption uneven - underscoring that NAM-generated data also require FAIR stewardship to be reusable.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A total of 68% (23/34) of the publications contained details on the outcomes of FAIRification endeavors and the expected future work.
findings.evidence: Body (Results) of a PRISMA-ScR scoping review of FAIR data stewardship initiatives across health research domains.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A total of 68% (23/34) of the publications contained details on the outcomes of FAIRification endeavors and the expected future work.
findings.study_system: FAIR data stewardship initiatives in health research (scoping review, 34 included studies)

findings.claim: Fewer than 10% of chemicals in commerce have been screened for safety, a data gap motivating both high-throughput NAMs and FAIR data infrastructure in environmental public health.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Out of the tens of thousands of individual chemicals currently in commerce (and many more mixtures, natural products, and metabolites) <10% have been screened for safety.
findings.evidence: Body (Introduction) of an expert perspective on bringing FAIR big data and AI/ML to environmental public health, co-authored by NICEATM leadership.
findings.effect_size: <10% of commercial chemicals screened for safety
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Out of the tens of thousands of individual chemicals currently in commerce (and many more mixtures, natural products, and metabolites) <10% have been screened for safety.
findings.study_system: environmental public health chemical safety data / FAIR + AI infrastructure

findings.claim: In FDA/CDER experience, NAM-based teratogenicity assays predicted teratogenicity of 75 known teratogens with 73-82% predictivity, improving to 88% when multiple assay platforms were combined.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Comparative analyses of these assays have been conducted using 75 known teratogens and demonstrated 73%−82% predictivity of teratogenicity.
findings.evidence: Body of an FDA/CDER/OND regulatory perspective quantifying NAM predictivity for teratogenicity against known reference teratogens.
findings.effect_size: 73-82% predictivity (75 known teratogens); up to 88% combined
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Comparative analyses of these assays have been conducted using 75 known teratogens and demonstrated 73%−82% predictivity of teratogenicity.
findings.study_system: NAM teratogenicity assays (MEFL/MESCA) vs 75 known teratogens

findings.claim: An industry survey found NAM-based regulatory filings replaced large-animal studies for biotherapeutic safety and were generally accepted by global health authorities.
findings.claim_source_sentence: These scientifically justified approaches were generally accepted by global health authorities, particularly in the context of species relevance limitations, prior target modulation experience, and/or when addressing severe disease.
findings.evidence: Biotechnology Innovation Organization survey/case studies of pharmaceutical-company NAM use in nonclinical safety assessment.
findings.study_system: pharmaceutical industry NAM regulatory filings (biotherapeutics)

findings.claim: A key barrier to replacing animal tests with NAMs in regulatory toxicology is the lack of standardized validation and acceptance criteria.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The transition from traditional animal testing to human-relevant New Approach Methods (NAMs) in regulatory toxicology faces a significant challenge: a lack of standardized validation and acceptance criteria.
findings.evidence: Review proposing a unified cross-industry framework for NAM validation and acceptance.
findings.study_system: regulatory toxicology NAM validation frameworks

findings.claim: Defining and applying acceptance criteria for the validity of each test run is essential for NAM use in toxicity testing; without them quality assurance has a blind spot.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The definition and application of acceptance criteria (AC) for the validity of test runs is important for the setup and use of test methods, particularly for the use of new approach methods (NAM) in toxicity testing.
findings.evidence: Methodological paper (part I) on acceptance criteria for NAMs in toxicology.
findings.study_system: NAM test-method acceptance criteria / quality assurance

findings.claim: Despite acknowledged benefits, real and perceived scientific, technical, legislative, economic and cultural barriers continue to limit NAM use in chemical safety decision-making.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Despite the widely acknowledged benefits offered by NAMs, there continue to be barriers that prevent or limit their application for decision-making in chemical safety assessment.
findings.evidence: Review of barriers to accelerated NAM adoption in chemical safety assessment.
findings.study_system: chemical safety assessment NAM adoption barriers

findings.claim: NAMs (in silico, in vitro, eleutheroembryo) are proposed to predict endocrine effects while reducing animal use, but uncertainties must be reduced before regulatory acceptance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: New approach methodologies (NAMs) hold great promise to identify molecular, cellular, and tissue changes that can be used to predict effects reliably and more efficiently at the individual level (and potentially on populations) while reducing the number of animals used in (eco)toxicological testing for endocrine disruption.
findings.evidence: Cross-sector review of NAMs for endocrine-activity assessment in fish and amphibians.
findings.study_system: ecotoxicology endocrine-activity NAMs (fish, amphibians)

findings.claim: Although many candidate NAMs have been developed, very few have been adopted for regulatory decision-making, prompting a UK roadmap for their acceptance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Many of these are potentially invaluable in the safety assessment of chemicals, but very few have been adopted for regulatory decision making.
findings.evidence: UK FSA/COT roadmap paper on development, endorsement and regulatory acceptance of NAMs.
findings.study_system: UK chemical risk assessment NAM roadmap

findings.claim: Across ICATM jurisdictions, non-animal alternatives for acute systemic toxicity are often not accepted, though several jurisdictions allow test waivers to reduce animal use.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For many jurisdictions and chemical sectors, non-animal alternatives are not accepted, but several jurisdictions provide guidance to support the use of test waivers to reduce animal use for specific applications.
findings.evidence: International review of regulatory uses of acute systemic toxicity data across ICATM member jurisdictions.
findings.study_system: international regulatory acute systemic toxicity testing (8 ICATM jurisdictions)

findings.claim: In the EU, guidance for predicting adversity with NAMs remains limited and endocrine-disruptor identification has largely depended on animal data - continued in vivo testing is required until alternatives are accepted.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, guidance on predicting adversity using NAMs remains limited, and ED identifications have largely depended on animal data to assess endocrine-mediated adversity.
findings.evidence: Review of the EU regulatory framework for endocrine disruptors and NAM use.
findings.study_system: EU endocrine-disruptor regulatory assessment (REACH, CLP, PPPR, BPR)

findings.claim: Regulatory uncertainty about NAM requirements induces companies to keep using traditional animal methods, slowing NAM development in Brazil.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The resulting regulatory uncertainty induces companies to keep on adopting the traditional methods, slowing NAM's development in the country.
findings.evidence: Perspective on the Brazilian regulatory context for NAM acceptance in product registration.
findings.study_system: Brazil regulatory NAM acceptance (pharma, devices, food, agrochemicals)

findings.claim: A US interagency working group found NAM adoption in regulatory decisions is slow and awareness outside the community is low, identifying five recurring barriers.
findings.claim_source_sentence: While the development and application of NAMs has recently increased, their adoption in regulatory decisions is slow and awareness outside the community is low.
findings.evidence: ICCVAM/CAMWG stakeholder-consultation paper on broadening NAM awareness and adoption.
findings.study_system: US interagency NAM adoption (agrochemical, industrial, consumer, pharma stakeholders)

findings.claim: Proponents argue NAMs are, in certain settings, entirely appropriate now for assuring chemical-ingredient safety within next-generation risk assessment, though regulatory adoption has been slow.
findings.claim_source_sentence: New approach methodologies (NAMs) that do not use experimental animals are, in certain settings, entirely appropriate for assuring the safety of chemical ingredients, although regulatory adoption has been slow.
findings.evidence: Opinion article advocating NAM/NGRA readiness for chemical safety assurance.
findings.study_system: next-generation risk assessment (NGRA) for chemical ingredients

findings.claim: A workshop identified in vitro/in silico alternatives that could waive the required 90-day dog study in agrochemical registration, pending international regulatory agreement.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Opportunities were identified to support alternative approaches to answer human safety questions without performing the required 90-day dog study.
findings.evidence: Workshop report on replacing dog studies in agrochemical evaluation with NAMs.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Opportunities were identified to support alternative approaches to answer human safety questions without performing the required 90-day dog study.
findings.study_system: agrochemical safety evaluation (dog studies)

findings.claim: Read-across is a validated NAM allowing in vivo tests to be waived under REACH, but three issues (similarity definition, activity translation, ADME differences) limit its regulatory acceptance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Three major issues were identified that need optimization to allow a higher regulatory acceptance rate of the RAx procedure: (i) the definition of similarity of source and target, (ii) the translation of biological/toxicological activity of source to target in the RAx procedure, and (iii) how to deal with issues of ADME that may differ between source and target.
findings.evidence: Expert workshop review on internationalizing read-across as a validated NAM.
findings.study_system: read-across (RAx) for regulatory toxicology (EU-REACH, OECD)

findings.claim: For human medicinal products, reduction and replacement of animal testing has been achieved through regulatory acceptance of new in vitro methods as pivotal, supportive or mechanistic studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: With respect to non-clinical testing requirements for human medicinal products, reduction and replacement of animal testing has been achieved by the regulatory acceptance of new in vitro methods, either as pivotal, supportive or exploratory mechanistic studies.
findings.evidence: Book chapter on regulatory acceptance of alternative methods in pharmaceutical development (EMA/ICH).
findings.study_system: pharmaceutical non-clinical testing 3Rs (EMA, ICH)

findings.claim: Microphysiological systems are expected to reduce drug-development costs by lowering compound attrition through more human-like in vitro physiology.
findings.claim_source_sentence: MPS will provide unprecedented human-like physiological properties of in vitro models, enabling their routine application in the pharma industry and thus reducing drug development costs by lowering the attrition rate of compounds.
findings.evidence: Editorial on cross-industrial applications of organotypic/MPS models.
findings.study_system: microphysiological systems across industry sectors

findings.claim: An organ-on-chip drug-response study detected drug-induced steatosis, with valproate producing a prolonged 15% rise in lipogenesis followed by mitochondrial stress.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Additionally, the authors observed that Stavudine exposure produced a brief increase in lipogenesis, whereas Valproate exposure resulted in a prolonged 15% rise in lipogenesis followed by mitochondrial stress, indicating a disruption in β-oxidation.
findings.evidence: Body (application examples) of a review of organ-on-chip technology, citing a liver-chip that quantitatively detected drug-induced lipogenesis changes.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Additionally, the authors observed that Stavudine exposure produced a brief increase in lipogenesis, whereas Valproate exposure resulted in a prolonged 15% rise in lipogenesis followed by mitochondrial stress, indicating a disruption in β-oxidation.
findings.study_system: organ-on-chip / microphysiological systems for drug testing

findings.claim: An intestinal-liver-on-chip reproduced acetaminophen absorption, toxicokinetics and hepatotoxicity, with the two-organ model remaining stable for 4 days.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Changes in liver injury biomarkers aspartate aminotransferase and alanine aminotransferase, and liver function marker albumin indicated that the short-term culture of the two organs-on-chip model was stable for 4 days.
findings.evidence: Primary study building an intestinal-liver MPS to simulate overdose acetaminophen hepatotoxicity.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Changes in liver injury biomarkers aspartate aminotransferase and alanine aminotransferase, and liver function marker albumin indicated that the short-term culture of the two organs-on-chip model was stable for 4 days.
findings.study_system: intestinal-liver-on-chip (Caco-2/HT29-MTX, HepG2/HUVEC/THP-1) acetaminophen model

findings.claim: A liver-on-chip genotoxicity NAM detected several genotoxicants in line with in vivo data, but failed to detect benzo[a]pyrene by two endpoints, indicating incomplete concordance and a need for optimization.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, B[a]P did not exhibit an increase in the % micronucleus and MF, which might require an optimization of the test system.
findings.evidence: Proof-of-principle primary study of a liver-on-chip MPS for predictive genotoxicity/mutagenicity.
findings.study_system: liver-on-chip MPS (primary hepatocytes/HepaRG + TK6) genotoxicity assays (4 reference genotoxicants)

findings.claim: In a dynamic liver-on-chip, hepatocytes maintained high viability for up to 15 days with robust albumin secretion, demonstrating sustained hepatic function of the MPS.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Hepatocytes in this setup maintained high viability for up to 15 days and exhibited robust albumin secretion.
findings.evidence: Body (Results) of a review of dynamic-fluid-flow liver-on-a-chip platforms, reporting sustained hepatocyte function.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Hepatocytes in this setup maintained high viability for up to 15 days and exhibited robust albumin secretion.
findings.study_system: liver-on-a-chip with dynamic fluid flow

findings.claim: Standard 2D-derived viability assays give inaccurate cellular-health readouts in 3D hydrogel constructs, a QC caveat for 3D-model toxicity data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Compared with direct cell viability commonly used in 2D cell culture, our results show cellular health output inaccuracies among each assay in differing hydrogel formulations.
findings.evidence: Primary comparative study of commercial viability assays in 3D hydrogel/organoid constructs.
findings.study_system: 3D hydrogel constructs / tumor organoids and spheroids (4 commercial viability assays compared)

findings.claim: Brain organoids enable modeling of human brain development and disease in a 3D environment, but have recognized limitations relative to other model systems.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This Roadmap article describes the features of brain organoids, focusing on the neocortex, and their advantages and limitations - in comparison with other model systems - for the study of brain development, evolution and disease.
findings.evidence: Roadmap review of brain organoids for modeling human brain development and disease.
findings.study_system: human pluripotent-stem-cell brain organoids (neocortex)

findings.claim: Mouse and rat kidneys differ substantially from human kidneys anatomically, histologically and molecularly, motivating human kidney organoids to predict drug toxicity more accurately than animal models.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Mouse or rat kidneys, however, differ substantially from human kidneys at the anatomical, histological, and molecular levels.
findings.evidence: Review of human reconstructed kidney models (organoids, kidney-on-chip).
findings.study_system: human kidney organoids vs rodent kidney models

findings.claim: A 3D inkjet-bioprinted alveolar lung-on-a-chip reproduced a thin multilayered barrier with epithelial tight junctions, key properties of the alveolar barrier.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The bioprinted models cultured on the chip maintained their structure with three layers of tens of micrometers and achieved a tight junction in the epithelial layer, the critical properties of an alveolar barrier.
findings.evidence: Primary study bioprinting a three-layer alveolar lung-on-a-chip.
findings.study_system: 3D inkjet-bioprinted alveolar lung-on-a-chip (four culture inserts)

findings.claim: Traditional chemical testing is too resource-intensive in time, money and animal use to evaluate all chemicals, motivating AOP-informed IATA for strategic testing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Current approaches are too resource intensive in terms of time, money and animal use to evaluate all chemicals under development or already on the market.
findings.evidence: Workshop summary on using Adverse Outcome Pathways to support IATA.
findings.study_system: AOP/IATA framework for regulatory chemical testing

findings.claim: QSAR and read-across for in vitro bacterial mutagenicity are reliable enough for prioritization and to support regulatory decisions with other evidence, but other genotoxicity endpoints need caution.
findings.claim_source_sentence: (Q)SAR models and read-across approaches for in vitro bacterial mutagenicity have sufficient reliability for use in prioritization processes, and as support in regulatory decisions in combination with other types of evidence.
findings.evidence: Review of in silico approaches for genotoxicity prediction in regulatory frameworks.
findings.study_system: in silico (Q)SAR/read-across genotoxicity prediction

findings.claim: Rodent cancer bioassays use hundreds of animals, are resource intensive and have limited human relevance; a weight-of-evidence framework is proposed to waive them for agrochemicals.
findings.claim_source_sentence: These studies use hundreds of animals, are resource intensive, and certain aspects of these studies have limited human relevance.
findings.evidence: Framework (ReCAAP) for waiving long-term rodent cancer bioassays via weight of evidence.
findings.effect_size: hundreds of animals per rodent cancer bioassay
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: These studies use hundreds of animals, are resource intensive, and certain aspects of these studies have limited human relevance.
findings.study_system: rodent chronic/carcinogenicity bioassays (agrochemicals)

findings.claim: Large fractions of regulated chemical inventories are complex/UVCB substances (about 25% of the US TSCA inventory), for which NAMs and read-across are needed for safety evaluation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Approximately 10% and 20% of substances registered under the EU chemicals legislation are 'multi-constituent substances' and 'substances of unknown or variable compositions, complex reaction products and biological substances' (UVCBs), respectively, and UVCBs comprise approximately 25% of the U.S. Toxic Substances Control Act Inventory.
findings.evidence: Workshop highlights on 21st-century NAM approaches for evaluating complex substances.
findings.effect_size: ~10% multi-constituent, ~20% UVCB (EU); ~25% of US TSCA inventory UVCB
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Approximately 10% and 20% of substances registered under the EU chemicals legislation are 'multi-constituent substances' and 'substances of unknown or variable compositions, complex reaction products and biological substances' (UVCBs), respectively, and UVCBs comprise approximately 25% of the U.S. Toxic Substances Control Act Inventory.
findings.study_system: complex substances / UVCBs regulatory NAM evaluation

findings.claim: The GRACIOUS framework uses IATA decision trees to justify grouping of nanoforms; several distance algorithms scored NF similarity comparably, reducing the need to test every nanoform.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The x-fold, Bayesian and Arsinh-OWA distance algorithms performed comparably in the scoring of similarity between NF pairs.
findings.evidence: White paper on quantitative similarity tools for grouping nanoforms within IATA.
findings.study_system: nanoform grouping / read-across (GRACIOUS IATA framework)

findings.claim: Two in silico phototoxicity tools (Derek Nexus, OECD QSAR Toolbox) predicted phototoxicity with moderate-to-high concordance against reference data, supporting non-animal phototoxicity screening.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Derek Nexus predicted phototoxicity of the compounds, with a sensitivity of 63%, specificity of 93%, Positive Predictive Values of 90% and Negative Predictive Value of 69%, overall accuracy of 77% and balanced accuracy of 78%.
findings.evidence: Primary evaluation of Derek Nexus and QSAR Toolbox for phototoxicity prediction against known outcomes.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Derek Nexus predicted phototoxicity of the compounds, with a sensitivity of 63%, specificity of 93%, Positive Predictive Values of 90% and Negative Predictive Value of 69%, overall accuracy of 77% and balanced accuracy of 78%.
findings.study_system: in silico phototoxicity prediction (Derek Nexus, OECD QSAR Toolbox)

findings.claim: A QSAR model classified FDA pregnancy risk category of antibiotics with 83.82% internal and 94.11% external accuracy, offering an in silico pre-screen where clinical/animal studies are ethically constrained.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The accuracy (ACC) values of the most successful model were 83.82% for the internal and 94.11% for the external validation.
findings.evidence: Primary QSAR modeling study predicting FDA pregnancy category of antibiotics.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The accuracy (ACC) values of the most successful model were 83.82% for the internal and 94.11% for the external validation.
findings.study_system: QSAR model of 97 antibiotics (FDA pregnancy categories)

findings.claim: Candidate Novichok structures may exceed 10,000 compounds, making experimental testing infeasible and motivating in silico QSAR estimation of hydrolysis and biodegradation (17 agents modeled).
findings.claim_source_sentence: After the CWC (Chemical Warfare Agent) list update, the candidate structures for the Novichoks may be over 10,000 compounds.
findings.evidence: Primary in silico study predicting environmental fate of Novichok agents.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: After the CWC (Chemical Warfare Agent) list update, the candidate structures for the Novichoks may be over 10,000 compounds.
findings.study_system: in silico QSAR (QSAR Toolbox, EPI Suite) for 17 Novichok agents

findings.claim: Machine-learning in silico toxicity models are limited by data quality, imbalance, activity cliffs and applicability-domain definition - challenges that must be addressed for reliable prediction.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Commonly overlooked challenges such as data imbalance, activity cliff, model evaluation, and definition of applicability domain are highlighted, and plausible solutions for alleviating these challenges are discussed.
findings.evidence: Review of machine-learning methods for in silico toxicity prediction.
findings.study_system: machine-learning SAR/QSAR toxicity prediction

findings.claim: A validated high-throughput assay screened the ToxCast phase I library (293 environmental chemicals) for sodium-iodide symporter inhibition to support development of thyroid adverse outcome pathways, expanding NAM coverage of thyroid molecular targets.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This study applied a previously validated high-throughput approach to screen for NIS inhibitors in the ToxCast phase I library, representing 293 important environmental chemicals.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract/Methods) of a primary high-throughput screening study of NIS inhibitors in ToxCast phase I, supporting thyroid AOP development for the US EPA Endocrine Disruptor Screening Program.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Here 310 blinded samples were screened in a tiered-approach using an initial single-concentration (100 μM) radioactive-iodide uptake (RAIU) assay, followed by 169 samples further evaluated in multi-concentration (0.001 μM-100 μM) testing in parallel RAIU and cell viability assays.
findings.study_system: high-throughput NIS-inhibition assay (ToxCast phase I) for thyroid AOP

findings.claim: Traditional in vivo water-quality benchmarks existed for only 34 of 67 chemicals monitored in Great Lakes tributaries, so ToxCast high-throughput bioactivity and AOPs were used to fill the data gap and prioritise chemicals of concern.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Traditional water-quality benchmarks for aquatic life based on in vivo toxicity data were available for 34 of 67 evaluated chemicals.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a primary environmental-monitoring study using ToxCast exposure-activity ratios and AOP-Wiki mapping to prioritise chemicals where in vivo benchmarks were missing.
findings.effect_size: 34 of 67 chemicals had in vivo benchmarks; 49 ToxCast assays aligned with 23 AOPs
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The 49 ToxCast assays prioritized via EAR analysis aligned with 23 potentially-relevant AOPs present in the AOP-Wiki.
findings.study_system: ToxCast HTS + AOP exposure-activity-ratio prioritization (57 Great Lakes tributaries)

findings.claim: A 'cytotoxic burst' confounds ToxCast high-throughput data - many assays only respond at cytotoxic concentrations - so pathway-specific NAM signals must be statistically distinguished from nonspecific effects before AOP development.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Previous work identified a "cytotoxic burst" (CTB) phenomenon wherein large numbers of the ToxCast assays begin to respond at or near test chemical concentrations that elicit cytotoxicity, and a statistical approach to defining the bounds of the CTB was developed.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a meta-analysis of ToxCast assay responses that prioritises target-specific assays for AOP development after accounting for nonspecific cytotoxicity.
findings.study_system: ToxCast HTS assay-response meta-analysis (AOP prioritization)

findings.claim: More than 80,000 chemicals in commerce challenge hazard assessment, motivating HTS-informed systems-toxicology models and AOPs (e.g., AOP43 vascular disruption) evaluated on a 38-chemical set of putative vascular-disrupting compounds as animal-free predictors of developmental toxicity.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The more than 80,000 chemicals in commerce present a challenge for hazard assessments that toxicity testing in the 21 century strives to address through high-throughput screening (HTS) assays.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a review/primary analysis modelling developmental vascular toxicity from ToxCast HTS data using an AOP and virtual-tissue systems toxicology.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: ToxCast HTS predictions from several published and unpublished assays covering different aspects of the angiogenic cycle were generated for a test set of 38 chemicals representing a range of putative vascular disrupting compounds (pVDCs).
findings.study_system: ToxCast HTS + AOP43 systems-toxicology model (developmental vascular toxicity)

findings.claim: Most ToxCast assays used cancer cell lines lacking integrated physiological functionality; a metabolically competent HepaRG toxicogenomic NAM screened 1060 chemicals across 93 gene transcripts to add physiology-relevant signal for AOP inference.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, most ToxCast screening assays have evaluated individual biological targets in cancer cell lines lacking integrated physiological functionality (such as receptor signaling, metabolism).
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a primary high-throughput toxicogenomic screen in metabolically competent HepaRG cells translating expression changes into Bayesian AOP-relevant inferences.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Expression of 93 gene transcripts was measured by quantitative polymerase chain reaction using Fluidigm 96.96 dynamic arrays in response to 1060 chemicals tested in eight-point concentration-response.
findings.study_system: HepaRG high-throughput toxicogenomic screening (metabolically competent hepatic NAM)

findings.claim: From 2171 chemicals with human hepatotoxicity classifications, only 157 of 1600+ ToxCast/Tox21 assays were associated with hepatotoxicity, grouped into 52 key-event models - illustrating how many biological events complex NAM toxicity prediction must integrate.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Using a database of 2171 chemicals with human hepatotoxicity classifications, we identified 157 out of 1600+ ToxCast/Tox21 HTS assays to be associated with human hepatotoxicity.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a computational-toxicology study building key-event models of hepatotoxicity from HTS data plus toxicokinetics.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Then, a computational framework was used to group these assays by biological target or mechanisms into 52 key event (KE) models of hepatotoxicity.
findings.study_system: ToxCast/Tox21 key-event modelling of human hepatotoxicity

findings.claim: A data-driven AOP for environmental cardiotoxicity was built by profiling high-throughput bioactivity of 4165 compounds active against VEGFR, proposing a computational route that could supplement and reduce the need for animal testing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: ToxCast, Tox21, and PubChem data were evaluated to obtain bioprofiles of 4165 compounds active in assays targeting VEGFR.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a data-driven study hypothesising an AOP linking VEGFR, endocrine disruption and atherosclerosis from HTS bioprofiles.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: By applying computational methods to profile HTS data and hypothesize a mechanistic AOP, this study proposes a data-driven approach to evaluating environmental cardiotoxicity, which could eventually supplement and reduce the need for animal testing in toxicological assessments.
findings.study_system: data-driven AOP from HTS bioprofiles (VEGFR / cardiotoxicity)

findings.claim: Integrating machine learning with PBPK modelling for NAM-based risk assessment is limited by the black-box nature and insufficient interpretability of many ML models.
findings.claim_source_sentence: due to the black box nature of many ML models, lack of sufficient interpretability is a limitation
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a review of ML/AI integration with PBPK modelling for drug development and chemical risk assessment.
findings.study_system: machine-learning/AI-integrated PBPK modelling for NAM risk assessment

findings.claim: In a high-throughput IVIVE workflow for developmental toxicity, only 7 of 23 chemicals with in vitro developmental-toxicity assays had a lower human oral equivalent dose from developmental assays than from all assays, so using all in vitro data was the most conservative NAM approach.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Of the 23 chemicals with in vitro developmental toxicity assays, 7 had a NAM-based human oral equivalent dose (hOED) that was lower for developmental assays than for all available assays, indicating that the use of all in vitro data to derive a hOED would generally provide the most conservative approach.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a study proposing an IVIVE workflow for prioritising potential developmental toxicants using reverse dosimetry and PBPK.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Of the 23 chemicals with in vitro developmental toxicity assays, 7 had a NAM-based human oral equivalent dose (hOED) that was lower for developmental assays than for all available assays, indicating that the use of all in vitro data to derive a hOED would generally provide the most conservative approach.
findings.study_system: high-throughput IVIVE workflow (developmental toxicity prioritization)

findings.claim: An IVIVE-pregnancy-PBPK NAM combining human embryonic stem-cell assays with modelling derived BPA reference doses (4.94 and 5.18 microg/kg/day) close to EFSA's 2015 temporary TDI, offering an animal-free risk-assessment strategy.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The results showed that simulated mean RfDs (µg/kg/day) derived from the HSD3B1 and NFATC2 gene of embryotoxicity and neurodevelopmental toxicity tests, respectively, were 4.94 and 5.18.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract/Results) of a primary IVIVE-P-PBPK study using human embryonic stem-cell toxicogenomics to derive BPA reference doses without animals.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The results showed that simulated mean RfDs (µg/kg/day) derived from the HSD3B1 and NFATC2 gene of embryotoxicity and neurodevelopmental toxicity tests, respectively, were 4.94 and 5.18.
findings.study_system: IVIVE-pregnancy-PBPK + hESC toxicogenomics (Bisphenol A)

findings.claim: A multi-agency review notes a burst of IVIVE publications and argues that replacing animal models via IVIVE requires a strategic plan to qualify these NAM methods for regulatory acceptance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In addition to refining and reducing the number of animals in traditional toxicity testing protocols and being used for prioritizing chemical testing, the goal to use IVIVE to facilitate the replacement of animal models can be achieved through their continued evolution and development, including a strategic plan to qualify IVIVE methods for regulatory acceptance.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a multi-agency (ICCVAM) review defining IVIVE and its regulatory decision-making applications.
findings.study_system: in vitro-to-in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) for regulatory risk assessment

findings.claim: Access to input parameters and the technical difficulty of applying and interpreting PBPK models has limited IVIVE as a routine part of in vitro NAM testing, motivating open-access computational tools (NIEHS Integrated Chemical Environment).
findings.claim_source_sentence: Thus, access to input parameters, as well as the technical requirements of applying and interpreting models, has limited the use of IVIVE as a routine part of testing.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a perspective describing open-access PBPK/IVIVE computational support tools in the Integrated Chemical Environment.
findings.study_system: open-access PBPK/IVIVE computational tools (ICE)

findings.claim: Life-stage-specific chemical risk assessment increasingly relies on NAMs (PBPK, BBDR, IVIVE), but existing gaps in toxicological datasets and modelling challenges must be overcome to expand their utility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We also discuss existing gaps in the available toxicological datasets and current challenges that need to be overcome to expand the utility of NAMs for life stage-specific chemical risk assessment.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a review of NAM-based life-stage-specific chemical risk assessment (FDA/NCTR).
findings.study_system: life-stage-specific NAM risk assessment (PBPK/IVIVE)

findings.claim: OECD Guideline 497 on defined approaches for skin sensitisation was the first OECD guideline of its kind, setting a precedent for regulatory adoption of NAMs performing equivalently to or better than animal tests.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This Defined Approach Guideline was the first of its kind for the OECD, and provides an important precedent for regulatory adoption of human biology-relevant new approach methodologies with performances equivalent to, or better than, traditional animal tests.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a mini-review on standardisation and international adoption of defined approaches under OECD Guideline 497.
findings.study_system: OECD Guideline 497 defined approaches (skin sensitisation)

findings.claim: No standardized in vitro assay exists for T-cell activation (key event 4) of the skin-sensitisation adverse outcome pathway, so this key event cannot be measured in vitro - a mechanistic-coverage gap for non-animal testing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: No standardized in vitro assays for T cell activation are available; thus, KE4 cannot be measured in vitro.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a review of non-animal skin-sensitisation test methods mapped to AOP key events.
findings.study_system: non-animal skin-sensitisation test methods (AOP key events)

findings.claim: OECD-adopted single non-animal skin-sensitisation methods, used in isolation, are insufficient to meet regulatory potency/hazard requirements comparable to animal tests, so defined approaches integrating multiple methods are needed.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Nevertheless, the currently adopted methods, when used in isolation, are not sufficient to fulfil regulatory requirements on the skin sensitisation potential and potency of chemicals comparable to that provided by the regulatory animal tests.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of an ICATM position paper on standardisation and international adoption of defined approaches for skin sensitisation.
findings.study_system: ICATM defined approaches for skin sensitisation (>20 regulatory authorities)

findings.claim: Because limitations of individual in chemico/in vitro/in silico assays carry through, OECD GL 497 defined approaches can give inconclusive skin-sensitisation predictions for borderline or out-of-domain chemicals, requiring weight-of-evidence resolution.
findings.claim_source_sentence: As limitations of the individual in chemico/in vitro assays and in silico predictions are carried through to the DAs, inconclusive predictions are possible for chemicals with results in the borderline range, and chemicals with out of domain results.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a case-study paper on resolving inconclusive defined-approach predictions with weight of evidence.
findings.study_system: OECD GL 497 defined approaches (2o3, ITS) - inconclusive-prediction case studies

findings.claim: A precondition for valid defined approaches is that reference data must not replicate the limitations of the murine local lymph node assay - warning that NAMs benchmarked against flawed animal reference data inherit those flaws.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The reference data should be selected to allow meaningful evaluations and must not replicate the limitations of the murine local lymph node assay (LLNA)
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a commentary on preconditions for implementing AOP-based defined approaches in OECD guidelines.
findings.study_system: AOP-based defined approaches implementation (skin sensitisation validation)

findings.claim: A mechanistic skin-sensitisation model benchmarked against human clinical data (diagnostic patch tests) rather than animal data is proposed as a new paradigm for quantitative risk assessment.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Furthermore, by benchmarking our mathematical model predictions against clinical datasets (e.g. human diagnostic patch test data), instead of animal test data, we propose that this approach could represent a new paradigm for mechanistic toxicology.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a paper applying the skin-sensitisation AOP to quantitative risk assessment via human-benchmarked mathematical models.
findings.study_system: mechanistic skin-sensitisation QRA models (human patch-test benchmarking)

findings.claim: The zebrafish embryo developmental toxicity assay protocol varies between laboratories, producing discordant data for identical compounds, and has low biotransformation capacity - reproducibility and standardization gaps for this NAM.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Unfortunately, the protocol of this zebrafish embryo assay varies between labs, resulting in discordant data for identical compounds.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a methods paper refining/standardising the zebrafish embryo developmental toxicity assay with metabolic activation and skeletal staining.
findings.study_system: zebrafish embryo developmental toxicity assay (ZEDTA) standardization

findings.claim: Calculated zebrafish embryo exposure (zAUC) for 14 drugs positive in the zebrafish developmental toxicity test correlated highly with rat, rabbit and human AUC, supporting zebrafish as an alternative to mammalian embryo-fetal development testing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The log of the calculated zAUC for the 14 drugs identified as positive in the zebrafish developmental toxicity test was relatively highly positively correlated with the log [AUC] for rats, rabbits, and humans.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a primary toxicokinetic study relating zebrafish embryo exposure to mammalian and human exposures for ICH S5 reference drugs.
findings.effect_size: 14 positive drugs (of 21 ICH S5 reference drugs)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We used this relationship to estimate the Ce values of the 21 positive-control reference drugs listed in ICH guidelines on reproductive and developmental toxicity studies (ICH S5).
findings.study_system: zebrafish embryo developmental toxicity test toxicokinetics (ICH S5 drugs)

findings.claim: The fish embryo toxicity test is supported as a replacement for the larval growth and survival test, with additional sublethal and gene-expression endpoints proposed to improve its predictive power.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The results not only show the utility of the fathead minnow FET test as a replacement for the LGS test but also provide evidence that inclusion of additional endpoints could improve the predictive power of the FET test.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a comparative primary study of FET vs larval growth-and-survival tests in fathead minnow and zebrafish.
findings.study_system: fish embryo toxicity test vs larval growth/survival test (zebrafish, fathead minnow)

findings.claim: QSAR and quantitative read-across (q-RASAR) models built on 133 pesticides/veterinary drugs met OECD validation thresholds and were combined to prioritise zebrafish-embryo developmental toxicity of untested chemicals without new animal testing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The QSAR model development adhered to rigorous OECD principles, ensuring that the model possessed good internal robustness (R> 0.6 and Q> 0.6) and external predictivity (R> 0.7, Q>0.7, and CCC> 0.85).
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a primary in silico QSAR/q-RASAR study predicting zebrafish embryo developmental toxicity for pesticides, veterinary drugs and bio-pesticides.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We collected 133 pesticides and veterinary drugs with half-maximal active concentration (AC) as the zebrafish embryo developmental toxicity endpoint.
findings.study_system: in silico QSAR/q-RASAR (zebrafish embryo developmental toxicity)

findings.claim: Zebrafish embryo behavioral assays detected neurotoxic effects of neonicotinoids that all correlated with mammalian study findings, supporting zebrafish embryos as an alternative developmental-neurotoxicity model.
findings.claim_source_sentence: All behavioral changes could be correlated to findings in mammalian studies.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a primary study of neonicotinoid developmental neurotoxicity in zebrafish embryo FET and behavioral assays.
findings.study_system: zebrafish embryo FET + coiling/swimming behavioral assays (neonicotinoids)

findings.claim: Despite academic hype, microphysiological systems had not been widely adopted by pharma nor reached regulated drug authorization; 46 experts identified assay-qualification level and stakeholder communication gaps as major barriers, creating a regulatory-acceptance dilemma.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Despite the MPS hype in academia and by platform providers, which says this technology is about to reshape the entire in vitro culture landscape in basic and applied research, MPS approaches have neither been widely adopted by the pharmaceutical industry yet nor reached regulated drug authorization processes at all.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a t4 workshop report by 46 experts from academia, MPS suppliers, pharma and regulators analysing MPS adoption barriers.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Here, 46 leading experts from all stakeholders - academia, MPS supplier industry, pharmaceutical and consumer products industries, and leading regulatory agencies - worldwide have analyzed existing challenges and hurdles along the MPS-based assay life cycle in a second workshop of this kind in June 2019.
findings.study_system: microphysiological systems industrial/regulatory adoption (t4 workshop)

findings.claim: By the 2023 t4 MPS workshop, academic MPS had matured but industrial adoption remained slow and the 2020 regulatory-acceptance recommendations were still not implemented, needing context-of-use qualification and standardization to make MPS data reliable.
findings.claim_source_sentence: It is concluded that communication between stakeholders has improved significantly, while the recommendations related to regulatory acceptance still need to be implemented.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of the 2023 t4 MPS workshop report reviewing progress against prior recommendations.
findings.study_system: microphysiological systems regulatory acceptance (2023 t4 workshop)

findings.claim: Barriers to effective data sharing among stakeholders and the lack of standardized data formats are named among key obstacles to MPS adoption, with standardized data formats proposed as a solution - underscoring that NAM data reusability, not just biology, gates progress.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Major challenges include standardization issues across terminology and protocols, validation complexities requiring robust reference compounds and benchmarking standards, regulatory uncertainties regarding data requirements and qualification processes, and barriers to effective data sharing among stakeholders.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of a path-forward paper on advancing MPS that proposes standardized data formats and pre-competitive consortia.
findings.study_system: microphysiological systems standardization and data sharing (CAAT)

findings.claim: FDA scientists note a gap in developing MPS from animal tissues; animal MPS could build confidence in human MPS data, enable comparison to in vivo animal data, and help identify species-specific effects, consistent with the 3Rs.
findings.claim_source_sentence: While there have been significant advances in the development, use, and proposals of qualification criteria for human organ MPS, there remains a gap in the development using animal tissues.
findings.evidence: Body (Abstract) of an FDA cross-center paper on the potential value of animal microphysiological systems.
findings.study_system: animal-tissue microphysiological systems (FDA regulatory value)

findings.claim: In a PRISMA systematic review of in silico NAMs (QSAR models) anchored in AOPs for thyroid-disruption-induced developmental neurotoxicity, only ~18% of 178 identified models met OECD (Q)SAR validation criteria in full, exposing a wide validation/quality gap in regulatory-ready in silico NAMs.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The fact that only 32 models (approximately 18%) achieved full compliance with the OECD QAF criteria serves as a critical benchmark for the field.
findings.evidence: Body (Discussion): quality assessment of 178 QSAR/in silico models against the OECD (Q)SAR Assessment Framework; only 32 fully compliant.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The fact that only 32 models (approximately 18%) achieved full compliance with the OECD QAF criteria serves as a critical benchmark for the field.
findings.study_system: in silico QSAR/NAMs for thyroid-disruption developmental neurotoxicity (systematic review of models)

findings.claim: A next-generation validation framework argues that validating NAMs by simple concordance with animal data is scientifically weak because many animal tests were themselves never validated for human relevance, motivating a shift to human-relevance-based validation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Moreover, simple concordance with animal data is a weak anchor because many animal tests were never validated for human relevance, and traditional validation often freezes a method at a single point in time despite rapid technological evolution.
findings.evidence: Body (Introduction/Discussion) of a next-generation validation framework for NGRA.
findings.study_system: regulatory validation frameworks for NAMs (conceptual/methodological)

findings.claim: Analysis of ECHA read-across submissions shows regulatory acceptance is uneven: category/group-based read-across is accepted far more often (~62%) than analogue read-across (~39%), indicating mechanistic grouping strengthens regulatory confidence in non-animal data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The acceptance rate is notably higher for group-based read-across approaches (about 62%) compared to analogue read-across types (about 39%).
findings.evidence: Body: comparative appraisal of EFSA 2025, ECHA RAAF and good read-across practice; reports ECHA acceptance statistics 2008-2023.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The acceptance rate is notably higher for group-based read-across approaches (about 62%) compared to analogue read-across types (about 39%).
findings.study_system: read-across (category vs analogue) regulatory submissions under REACH

findings.claim: The MechoA+ structural-alert profiler predicts mechanism of toxic action for chemical safety with 92% correctly assigned on its clear-outcome training set, supporting mechanism-based read-across/grouping as a NAM for both mammalian and ecotoxicity.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The combined results of the “Overall validity” are presented inbelow: Thus, on 1502 substances with a “clear” outcome in the training set (1383 Valid, 119 Invalid), 92% may be considered well predicted (TP) and 8% wrongly assigned (FP).
findings.evidence: Body (Results): validity of MechoA+ predictions on 1502 training-set substances with clear outcomes.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The combined results of the “Overall validity” are presented inbelow: Thus, on 1502 substances with a “clear” outcome in the training set (1383 Valid, 119 Invalid), 92% may be considered well predicted (TP) and 8% wrongly assigned (FP).
findings.study_system: in silico mechanism-of-toxic-action profiling (mammalian + ecotox) for chemicals

findings.claim: A chemical-agnostic Bayesian hierarchical calibration of quantitative AOPs yields wider 95% probability intervals that better cover observed dose-response data than a flat pooled model, improving uncertainty quantification for qAOP-based next-generation risk assessment.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Although the mean curves remain similar, the 95% probability intervals of the hierarchical model (blue ribbon) are wider and provide substantially better coverage of the data compared with the flat model (red ribbon).
findings.evidence: Body (Results): hierarchical vs flat qAOP calibration on a nonmutagenic liver-tumor case study (10 chemicals, 11 studies).
findings.effect_size: hierarchical 95% probability intervals give better data coverage than flat model
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Although the mean curves remain similar, the 95% probability intervals of the hierarchical model (blue ribbon) are wider and provide substantially better coverage of the data compared with the flat model (red ribbon).
findings.study_system: quantitative adverse outcome pathway (qAOP) calibration; liver-tumor case study

findings.claim: A review of human PSC-derived organoids for drug discovery sets assay-quality benchmarks (coefficient of variation <20% acceptable, <10% optimal), underscoring that reproducibility metrics, not only biological fidelity, gate organoid adoption in screening.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In terms of pharmacology, general best practices for assay development indicate that a coefficient of variation (CV), reflecting the size of a standard deviation relative to its mean, < 20% is acceptable, and CV < 10% is an optimal quality criterion (;;).
findings.evidence: Body: assay quality criteria for organoid-based high-throughput screening.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In terms of pharmacology, general best practices for assay development indicate that a coefficient of variation (CV), reflecting the size of a standard deviation relative to its mean, < 20% is acceptable, and CV < 10% is an optimal quality criterion (;;).
findings.study_system: human pluripotent stem cell-derived organoids for drug discovery / HTS

findings.claim: Framing human intestinal organoids as FDA New Approach Methodologies, the authors note only ~15% of IBD drug candidates entering phase I are ultimately approved despite >700 active trials, arguing human-relevant organoids are needed to reduce preclinical-to-clinical attrition.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Despite more than 700 active clinical trials registered, only about 15% of IBD drug candidates that enter phase I are ultimately approved [,].
findings.evidence: Body (Introduction): drug attrition statistics motivating intestinal organoids as NAMs.
findings.effect_size: ~15% of phase I IBD candidates approved; >700 active trials
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Despite more than 700 active clinical trials registered, only about 15% of IBD drug candidates that enter phase I are ultimately approved [,].
findings.study_system: human intestinal organoids as NAMs (inflammatory bowel disease drug discovery)

findings.claim: An intestinal-organoid-derived mathematical model coupled to PBPK predicted clinical incidence of any-grade and grade->=3 diarrhea for oral oncology drugs, with maximum predicted probabilities closely matching reported clinical rates, demonstrating organoid NAMs quantitatively predicting human toxicity.
findings.claim_source_sentence: When comparing predictions alongside observations, the maximum predicted probability of diarrhea during the course of treatment, expressed as a percentage, closely matched the clinically reported diarrhea incidence of any grade and of grade 3 or higher (Table).
findings.evidence: Body (Results): organoid-based probabilistic model predictions vs clinical diarrhea incidence.
findings.effect_size: predicted maximum diarrhea probability closely matched clinical incidence (any grade and grade >=3)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: When comparing predictions alongside observations, the maximum predicted probability of diarrhea during the course of treatment, expressed as a percentage, closely matched the clinically reported diarrhea incidence of any grade and of grade 3 or higher (Table).
findings.study_system: human intestinal organoid + PBPK model predicting oncology-drug GI toxicity

findings.claim: In an early-stage MPS qualification case study, a blood-perfused Vessel-on-Chip required donor-specific control thresholds (<2% area for negative, >4% for positive controls) to manage inter-donor variability, illustrating that context-of-use qualification governs MPS reproducibility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: To manage this, we established clear thresholds for platelet aggregation: <2% culture area covered for negative controls and >4% coverage for positive controls before including experimental data from a particular blood donor.
findings.evidence: Body (Results): platelet-aggregation control thresholds set to handle blood-donor variability in Vessel-on-Chip qualification.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: To manage this, we established clear thresholds for platelet aggregation: <2% culture area covered for negative controls and >4% coverage for positive controls before including experimental data from a particular blood donor.
findings.study_system: blood-perfused Vessel-on-Chip microphysiological system (qualification case study)

findings.claim: A liver-MPS qualification roadmap reports a human liver microphysiological model with 100% sensitivity and 90% specificity for drug-induced liver injury, while proposing ICC-based reproducibility grading (excellent ICC>=0.8) to standardize primary-hepatocyte qualification.
findings.claim_source_sentence: It provides a model that more accurately reflects human biology than traditional approaches, with a reported sensitivity of 100% and specificity of 90% for predicting drug-induced liver injury (DILI) [].
findings.evidence: Body: reported DILI predictive performance and reproducibility (ICC) classification scheme.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: It provides a model that more accurately reflects human biology than traditional approaches, with a reported sensitivity of 100% and specificity of 90% for predicting drug-induced liver injury (DILI) [].
findings.study_system: human liver microphysiological system (primary hepatocyte qualification for DILI)

findings.claim: A review of organs-on-chips in drug development reports proximal-tubule-on-chip clearance estimates typically within 10-20% RMSE of clinical values after IVIVE scaling, evidencing quantitative human concordance of MPS for renal drug handling.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Proximal tubule-on-a-chip platforms quantify active and passive renal clearance, transporter-mediated drug–drug interactions, and nephrotoxicity, with chip-derived clearance estimates typically within 10–20% RMSE of clinical values after IVIVE scaling [,].
findings.evidence: Body: quantitative performance of proximal-tubule-on-chip vs clinical clearance.
findings.effect_size: within 10-20% RMSE of clinical clearance values (after IVIVE)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Proximal tubule-on-a-chip platforms quantify active and passive renal clearance, transporter-mediated drug–drug interactions, and nephrotoxicity, with chip-derived clearance estimates typically within 10–20% RMSE of clinical values after IVIVE scaling [,].
findings.study_system: proximal tubule-on-a-chip (renal clearance / nephrotoxicity)

findings.claim: A PRISMA systematic cross-sector review of regulatory NAMs for developmental and reproductive toxicity (DART) narrowed 1155 screened articles to 92 included studies, mapping where NAMs are and are not accepted across regulatory sectors for DART.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Ultimately, 92 studies met the inclusion criteria and were incorporated into the qualitative synthesis and regulatory analysis presented in this review.
findings.evidence: Body (Methods): PRISMA selection funnel of the systematic review.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Ultimately, 92 studies met the inclusion criteria and were incorporated into the qualitative synthesis and regulatory analysis presented in this review.
findings.study_system: systematic review of NAMs for developmental & reproductive toxicity (DART) regulation

findings.claim: A review of in vitro NAM data for chemical risk assessment identifies lack of harmonization across NAM assays, platforms, data standards and analytical pipelines as a persistent barrier to regulatory adoption, directly linking NAM uptake to data standardization/FAIR stewardship.
findings.claim_source_sentence: 4.3 Limited harmonization A persistent barrier to widespread regulatory adoption is the lack of harmonization across NAM assays, platforms, data standards, and analytical pipelines.
findings.evidence: Body (Bottlenecks): harmonization/data-standards barrier to regulatory NAM adoption.
findings.study_system: in vitro NAM data application to chemical risk assessment (NGRA)

findings.claim: A cardiotoxicity AOP network analysis finds its constituent AOPs are largely immature: most are still under development (30.76%) or not yet formally evaluated (46.15%), showing that AOP frameworks underpinning NAMs remain mostly non-validated.
findings.claim_source_sentence: One was under review (AOP: 456), while the remaining are still under development (30.76%) or have not yet undergone formal evaluation (46.15%).
findings.evidence: Body (Results): formal evaluation/maturity status of AOPs in the cardiotoxicity network.
findings.effect_size: 30.76% under development, 46.15% not yet formally evaluated
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: One was under review (AOP: 456), while the remaining are still under development (30.76%) or have not yet undergone formal evaluation (46.15%).
findings.study_system: adverse outcome pathway network for cardiotoxicity (AOP-Wiki)

findings.claim: The CHIASMA animal-free chemical-safety framework standardizes NAM documentation via ToxTemp/SPSF templates aligned to OECD GD 211 and GIVIMP, operationalizing harmonized, regulatory-ready reporting so NAM data are reusable across a 23-partner consortium.
findings.claim_source_sentence: To ensure transparency and harmonization, CHIASMA partners employ standardized documentation tools, including the ToxTemp templateand the SPSF, as described in OECD GD 211 and the Good In Vitro Method Practices (GIVIMP) guidance.
findings.evidence: Body (Project Description): standardized documentation/reporting tools for NAM harmonization.
findings.study_system: multi-tiered animal-free NAM framework for REACH/CLP chemical safety (CHIASMA consortium)

findings.claim: A nanosafety metadata-stewardship paper argues NAM/nanosafety data need FAIR-aligned metadata captured at the point of generation plus dedicated 'data shepherd' roles, offering 8 recommendations to make experimental data findable and reusable.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Finally, we provide 8 key recommendations regarding the next steps to facilitate the widespread implementation of metadata reporting, and highlight some key tools and approaches that are facilitating the transition to capturing data and metadata much earlier in the data lifecycle, i.e., at the point of data generation.
findings.evidence: Body (Conclusions): recommendations for early metadata capture and stewardship of nanosafety/NAM data.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Finally, we provide 8 key recommendations regarding the next steps to facilitate the widespread implementation of metadata reporting, and highlight some key tools and approaches that are facilitating the transition to capturing data and metadata much earlier in the data lifecycle, i.e., at the point of data generation.
findings.study_system: nanosafety/NAM data metadata stewardship (FAIR data infrastructure)

findings.claim: A human vessel-chip IND-enabling study notes the FDA Modernization Acts 2.0 and 3.0 now allow MPS to be used alongside or instead of animal models in IND submissions, and stresses that a precisely specified context-of-use (clinical use plus target demographic) is required for regulatory readiness.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The FDA Modernization Acts 2.0 and 3.0 have changed the rulebook by allowing non‐animal methods, such as MPS, to be used alongside or instead of animal models in IND submissions.
findings.evidence: Body: regulatory positioning of vessel-chip MPS for IND submissions and context-of-use specification.
findings.study_system: human vessel-chip microphysiological system (IND-enabling; thrombosis/vascular)

findings.claim: In an oral-biopharmaceutics NAM review, intestinal organoids are shown to reproduce crypt-villus architecture and express clinically relevant drug transporters (MDR1, BCRP, PEPT1) and CYP3A4 that are absent or poorly represented in conventional Caco-2 monolayers, giving organoids greater human relevance for absorption prediction.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Intestinal organoids reproduce crypt-villus architecture and express clinically relevant transporters (MDR1, BCRP, and PEPT1) and enzymes (CYP3A4), which are absent or poorly represented in conventional monolayers [].
findings.evidence: Body: comparison of intestinal organoids vs Caco-2 monolayers for transporter/enzyme expression.
findings.study_system: intestinal organoids vs Caco-2 monolayers (oral drug absorption NAMs)

findings.claim: A preclinical-oncology NAM review reports patient-derived colorectal organoids predicted individual clinical responses to cetuximab with >80% concordance to patient outcomes, evidencing organoids as human-relevant predictors in a field where >90% of oncology candidates that pass animal testing fail in trials.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For example, patient-derived colorectal organoids have predicted individual clinical responses to cetuximab with >80% concordance to patient outcomes [].
findings.evidence: Body: patient-derived organoid concordance with clinical drug response.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: For example, patient-derived colorectal organoids have predicted individual clinical responses to cetuximab with >80% concordance to patient outcomes [].
findings.study_system: patient-derived colorectal cancer organoids (clinical drug-response prediction)

findings.claim: A next-generation-toxicology review of in vivo study variability finds that even standardized animal reference assays are imperfectly reproducible: the Hershberger and uterotrophic assays showed replicability of only 72% and 74% respectively, undermining animal-test concordance as the benchmark for validating NAMs.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The Hershberger and uterotrophic assays gave similar degrees of replicability: 72% and 74%, respectively (;).
findings.evidence: Body (Results): quantitative replicability of standardized in vivo endocrine assays.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The Hershberger and uterotrophic assays gave similar degrees of replicability: 72% and 74%, respectively (;).
findings.study_system: variability/replicability of standardized in vivo (animal) toxicology assays

findings.claim: A review of organ-on-a-chip technology quantifies a core reproducibility limit: liver-chip urea-production coefficient of variation rose from below 5% on day 1 to 20% by day 7 across hepatocyte donors, exposing donor-to-donor variability as an ongoing barrier even as the first OOC (Emulate Liver-Chip) was accepted into the FDA ISTAND pilot in 2024.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The liver-chip systems maintained a coefficient of variation below 5% for urea production on day 1, increasing to 20% by day 7 across different hepatocyte donors,highlighting ongoing challenges with donor-to-donor variability in primary human cells.
findings.evidence: Body: donor variability metrics for liver-chip urea production over time.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The liver-chip systems maintained a coefficient of variation below 5% for urea production on day 1, increasing to 20% by day 7 across different hepatocyte donors,highlighting ongoing challenges with donor-to-donor variability in primary human cells.
findings.study_system: liver-on-chip microphysiological system (primary human hepatocyte reproducibility)

findings.claim: At an EU cosmetics-safety workshop, a NAM bioactivity toolbox coupled to PBK modelling was shown to give an equivalent level of protection to a stand-alone rat repeat-dose toxicity study across 46 benchmark chemical exposures, evidencing animal-free systemic safety assessment.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: New approach methodologies (NAMs) that do not use experimental animals are, in certain settings, entirely appropriate for assuring the safety of chemical ingredients, although regulatory adoption has been slow.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: However, guidance on predicting adversity using NAMs remains limited, and ED identifications have largely depended on animal data to assess endocrine-mediated adversity.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Regulatory readiness of NAMs: proponents assert NAMs are already fit to assure chemical safety in certain settings, whereas the EU endocrine-disruptor review documents continued dependence on animal data because NAM adversity-prediction guidance is still limited.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: The inefficiency of existing animal models to precisely predict human pharmacological effects is the root reason for drug development failure.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Compared with direct cell viability commonly used in 2D cell culture, our results show cellular health output inaccuracies among each assay in differing hydrogel formulations.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Human-relevance/reliability of 3D NAMs: organ-on-chip advocates present the platforms as superior human-relevant replacements for animals, while a QC study shows standard readout assays give inaccurate results in 3D constructs, questioning the reliability of 3D-model toxicity data.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Switching to liver-on-chip for DILI evaluations could save approximately $3 billion annually by enhancing productivity through earlier and more reliable predictions.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Despite the widely acknowledged benefits offered by NAMs, there continue to be barriers that prevent or limit their application for decision-making in chemical safety assessment.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Projected efficiency benefits vs adoption reality: modelling projects multi-billion-dollar savings from NAM adoption, while barrier analyses show scientific, regulatory, economic and cultural obstacles keep NAMs from being adopted in practice.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: (Q)SAR models and read-across approaches for in vitro bacterial mutagenicity have sufficient reliability for use in prioritization processes, and as support in regulatory decisions in combination with other types of evidence.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: However, B[a]P did not exhibit an increase in the % micronucleus and MF, which might require an optimization of the test system.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Concordance of NAM genotoxicity data with in vivo: in silico bacterial-mutagenicity NAMs are judged reliable, but an experimental liver-on-chip genotoxicity NAM missed a known genotoxicant on two endpoints, showing endpoint-dependent, incomplete concordance.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: This Defined Approach Guideline was the first of its kind for the OECD, and provides an important precedent for regulatory adoption of human biology-relevant new approach methodologies with performances equivalent to, or better than, traditional animal tests.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: As limitations of the individual in chemico/in vitro assays and in silico predictions are carried through to the DAs, inconclusive predictions are possible for chemicals with results in the borderline range, and chemicals with out of domain results.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Performance of defined-approach NAMs for skin sensitisation: one paper presents OECD Guideline 497 defined approaches as equal-or-better replacements for animal tests, while the other shows the DAs inherit their component assays' limitations and yield inconclusive predictions for borderline/out-of-domain chemicals.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: These technologies bioengineer aspects of organ architecture and functionality, revolutionizing drug development, reducing animal testing, and enabling personalized medicine approaches.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: MPS approaches have neither been widely adopted by the pharmaceutical industry yet nor reached regulated drug authorization processes at all.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Transformative promise vs adoption reality for microphysiological systems: one frames MPS as already revolutionizing drug development and reducing animal use, while the expert workshop documents that MPS are not widely adopted by pharma and have not entered regulated drug authorization.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: The consensus of the expert panel was that the DNT IVB might be used during initial screening, but it is not presently a complete or surrogate approach to determine whether a chemical is a DNT in humans.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: This case study using FRs suggests that human cell-based DNT in vitro battery is a promising approach for neurodevelopmental hazard assessment and compound prioritization in risk assessment.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Disagreement on the regulatory readiness of the human developmental-neurotoxicity in vitro battery: an expert panel judges it insufficient as a stand-alone/surrogate hazard-classification tool and needing more validation, whereas a data-generating group presents it as a promising approach already usable for hazard assessment and prioritization.

evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Large, independent, cross-laboratory validation studies quantifying NAM predictive concordance against human outcomes (not just against animal tests) across many chemicals/endpoints
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Regulatory acceptance hinges on demonstrated human-relevant predictivity; most quantitative claims come from single-lab proof-of-concept studies

evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: NAM-specific data standards, ontologies and repositories; existing FAIR literature is dominated by clinical/omics health data, not organ-on-chip/QSAR/HTS outputs
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Without FAIR curation, the high-dimensional data NAMs generate cannot be reused, pooled for validation, or fed to in silico models - re-creating the reuse failures seen with animal data

evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Standardized acceptance criteria and QC assays validated for 3D constructs; evidence that 2D-derived assays mislead in 3D
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Unreliable readouts undermine the toxicity data used to justify replacing animal studies

evidence_gaps.topic: FAIR stewardship of NAM and AOP mechanistic data
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Mature, consensus technical tools and metadata standards to make NAM/AOP data findable, interoperable and reusable are still being established rather than routinely applied.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Without FAIRified NAM data, the mechanistic evidence generated to replace animal testing cannot be efficiently reused across labs or credibly integrated into next-generation risk assessment.

evidence_gaps.topic: Material-driven artefacts in organ-on-chip / MPS measurements
evidence_gaps.what_is_missing: Standardized correction for PDMS adsorption/absorption of small molecules across MPS platforms; most studies report ad hoc protocols for single compounds.
evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Uncorrected compound loss to device materials biases ADME and toxicity readouts, undermining reproducibility and regulatory confidence in MPS-derived NAM data.

strongest_evidence.claim: Quantitative in silico predictive-performance metrics (e.g., phototoxicity accuracy 77-79%; QSAR pregnancy-category accuracy up to 94.11%; QSAR-ICE aquatic models >75% cross-validation success) demonstrate NAMs can reach usable predictivity for specific, well-defined endpoints.
strongest_evidence.why_strong: Numbers are reported directly in abstracts/full text with defined validation sets and metrics; multiple independent studies converge on moderate-to-high predictivity for narrow endpoints.

weakest_evidence_cited.claim: Broad claims that NAMs/organ-on-chip are ready human-relevant replacements for animal models.
weakest_evidence_cited.why_weak: Largely from single-lab proof-of-concept studies, reviews and opinion pieces without independent cross-lab validation; contradicted by QC-accuracy and endpoint-concordance failures and by continued regulatory reliance on animal data.
